pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: TRICKSTER NARRATIVES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why would we listen to trickster narratives?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main events in trickster narratives
2. appreciate the importance of trickster narratives in the inculcation of values

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: TRICKSTER NARRATIVES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: TRICKSTER NARRATIVES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the main events in trickster narratives

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the main events in trickster narratives. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the main events in trickster narratives.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the main events in trickster narratives. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of trickster narratives in the inculcation of values

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of trickster narratives in the inculcation of values. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of trickster narratives in the inculcation of values.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of trickster narratives in the inculcation of values. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the main events in trickster narratives)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance of trickster narratives in the inculcation of values)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the main events in trickster narratives.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of trickster narratives in the inculcation of values.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why would we listen to trickster narratives?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the main events in trickster narratives.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of trickster narratives in the inculcation of values.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
